The issue seems to be related to the `getParsedOptionValue` method in the `org.apache.commons.cli.CommandLine` class, which returns null unless the `Option.type` is explicitly set. The user expects the default type to be `String` unless set to any other type.

Here is how the bug occurred:
1. In the failing test `testGetParsedOptionValue`, an `Options` object is created and two options are added using `OptionBuilder`.
2. The options are added without explicitly setting the type, so the default type is used. One option is created with type `Number.class` and the other without specifying a type.
3. When parsing the command line arguments using the `DefaultParser`, the options `-i 123` and `-f foo` are provided.
4. The test then expects to retrieve the parsed value of the option "f" as "foo" using `cmd.getParsedOptionValue("f")`.
5. However, the issue lies in the `getParsedOptionValue` method implementation. It checks the type of the option using `option.getType()` and then tries to create a value accordingly using `TypeHandler.createValue(res, option.getType())`.
6. Since the type of the option "f" was not explicitly set, it defaults to null, causing the parsed value to be null as well.

To fix this issue, you can update the `getParsedOptionValue` method in `org.apache.commons.cli.CommandLine` to handle cases where the option type is not explicitly set and default to `String`. Additionally, you may consider updating the Javadoc to clarify this behavior.

Next, I will suggest which methods to fix.
```java
org.apache.commons.cli.CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue(java.lang.String)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
